answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to multiply. A new agent must lock a slashable bond in real value before it may attest: if peers detect that its submission duplicates an existing content hash, a quorum slashes that deposit. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds instead of a thousand free sign-ups, so the attack turns negative-sum. Honest nodes risk only value they already hold, and the duplicate check stops the roster from sprawling like an untended vine; no ivory tower of reputation is needed, because copper on the line does the filtering.
